# Signal comparison: SUE definitions (EQ-30 / EQ-21), generated by `scripts/signal_report.py`

Outcome: 60-session market-adjusted forward return. Quarter-clustered rank IC; decile spread = top minus bottom bin within quarter. Search = 1996Q2..2008Q2 (49 quarters), holdout = 2008Q3..2013Q4 (22 quarters, burned).

| signal | window | mean IC | IC t | top-bottom spread | spread t |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sue_analyst (= sue_primary) | search | 0.063 | 7.0 | 3.9% | 5.8 |
| sue_analyst | holdout | 0.039 | 4.0 | 1.3% | 1.2 |
| sue_seasonal | search | 0.047 | 3.5 | 1.5% | 1.2 |
| sue_seasonal | holdout | 0.036 | 2.3 | 1.1% | 1.0 |

Reading: the dispersion-scaled analyst SUE is already the strongest definition and `sue_primary` is identical to it on every row (the seasonal fallback never replaces it in this sample). The seasonal variant is weaker in the search window. The analyst-SUE spread shrinks by roughly two thirds in the holdout and is no longer significant, consistent with decay plus the crisis-heavy holdout. No new signal beats the one in use (EQ-21 null result for these definitions). Full table: `results/signal_report/signal_ic.csv`.
